title: Traffic policy simulator and LTS-aware rollout gambit
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a traffic-policy simulator + controller that lets release engineers define LTS-channel aware rollout policies and run realistic simulated ramps before touching production. Goals: 1) let PM/Release own a declarative policy (percent schedule, health gates, fallback variants, feature-flag scope), 2) simulate traffic shape, error spikes, and latency regressions to score risk, 3) produce an actionable plan and a machine-readable rollout manifest that the rollout controller can execute and auto-rollback if SLOs breach. This ticket covers spec, toy sim engine, CI validation harness, and ops runbook for first internal LTS migration (1.9 -> 2.0).
acceptance_criteria: Declarative policy DSL is documented and supports: target cohorts, percent ramps, health gates (p50/p95 error rate), time windows, LTS channel overrides, and feature-flag scoping
Simulator can ingest traffic profiles (steady, burst, ramp, chaotic) and inject faults/latency from a parameterized fault library
Simulator outputs a risk score and recommended rollout curve for given policy + traffic profile
Controller consumes rollout manifest and enforces percent ramps with live telemetry checks and automatic rollback when gates fail
End-to-end demo run performed for LTS migration plan with post-mortem and runbook completed
